newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police arrest notorious criminal again.
newsitem.headline: Indian police arrest notorious criminal again.

text.p: Indian police arrested renowned criminal Charles Sobhraj on Monday, minutes after a judge ordered him released on bail after more than two decades in prison, his lawyers said.

Dozens of police surrounded Sobhraj as he left a courtroom in New Delhi after chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar ordered him released. "They have again arrested him because he did not have any valid documents," lawyer Amit Sharma said.
Sharma said Sobhraj's legal team planned to move a case of contempt of court against Delhi police.
Surrounded by police but without handcuffs, Sobhraj, 52, was put into a police van and driven away. It was not known where he was taken.

A French citizen born to an Indian father and a Vietnamese mother, Sobhraj told reporters last week that he feared re-arrest as he did not have valid papers authorising him to remain in India as a foreigner.
He had said he planned to go directly from the court to the French embassy to obtain papers after being released on bail.
